Here’s a 1‑week deload that keeps the same exercise menu and movement order your client has been running, but meaningfully reduces volume and intensity to shed fatigue while maintaining technical sharpness. Assumes a typical 4-day upper/lower split; if his split differs, apply the same reductions to each session.

Deload principles applied
- Volume: 40–60% of prior working sets per exercise (target: ~8–10 total working sets per session vs. 18).
- Intensity: RPE 6–7 on all sets; leave 3–4 reps in reserve on compounds, 2–3 RIR on accessories.
- Tempo and control: Smooth, controlled eccentrics (2–3 sec), no grinding, no forced reps, no failure.
- Rest: 2–3 min on compounds, 60–90 sec on accessories.
- Keep the same exercises and order he used last block.

Weekly structure
- Frequency: Same as previous week (example below uses 4 sessions).
- Load selection: Start ~80–85% of last week’s loads on compounds, ~75–80% on accessories; adjust set-to-set to stay within RPE 6–7.
- Warm-up: Fewer ramp sets than usual; 2–3 quick build-up sets to first working load.

Example 4-day split deload

Day 1 – Upper (horizontal emphasis)
- Bench press (same variant as block): 3 sets × 3–5 reps @ RPE 6
- Barbell or DB row: 3 × 6–8 @ RPE 6–7
- Incline DB press: 2 × 8–10 @ RPE 6–7
- Chest-supported row or cable row: 2 × 10–12 @ RPE 6–7
- Lateral raises: 2 × 12–15 @ RPE 6–7
- Triceps pressdown or skull crushers: 1–2 × 10–12 @ RPE 6–7
- Biceps curl (same variant): 1–2 × 10–12 @ RPE 6–7

Day 2 – Lower (squat emphasis)
- Back squat (same variant): 3 × 3–5 @ RPE 6

- Split squat or leg press: 2 × 8–10 @ RPE 6–7
- Leg curl: 2 × 10–12 @ RPE 6–7
- Calf raise: 2 × 10–12 @ RPE 6–7
- Optional core (plank or carry): 1–2 sets easy, stop well short of fatigue

Day 3 – Rest or active recovery
- 20–30 min easy Zone 2 cardio or a 30–45 min walk, mobility 10–15 min

Day 4 – Upper (vertical/push-pull emphasis)

Day 5 – Lower (deadlift/hinge emphasis)

Notes on progression during deload week
- If RPE drifts above 7, reduce load or cut a set. If it feels too easy (RPE <6), add 2–3% load next set, but do not exceed RPE 7.
- Stop all sets with perfectly clean reps. No grinders, no paused/max-effort work unless that is the exercise’s standard form.
- Keep total work sets per session about 8–10. If his normal day had different exercises, mirror this set scheme across them.

Accessory superset option
- To shorten sessions and keep flow: pair complementary accessories (e.g., lateral raise with triceps pressdown) while keeping RPE targets.

Recovery focus for the week
- Sleep: 7.5–9 hours/night; consistent bed/wake times.
- Steps and light cardio: Maintain 6–10k steps/day; 1–2 easy Zone 2 sessions (20–30 min).
- Mobility: 10–15 min easy mobility after sessions for hips, T-spine, shoulders.

- Deload mindset: This is practice week—reaffirm technique cues, bar path, bracing, and set-up rituals. Finish each session feeling better than you started.

Return-to-intensification guidance
- After deload, resume the intensification block at normal frequency. Start week 1 loads around the last mesocycle’s top sets minus 2–3% (or same load with 1–2 fewer reps) and climb across the block. Use the deload’s crisp technique as the baseline standard for harder work.

  3) Keep at deload prescription (2–3 × 6–8 @ RPE 6–7).

- No AMRAPs, no max testing, no grinders, no extra accessory volume.

- These exposures maintain neural drive and skill without building meaningful fatigue, so you still get the deload’s recovery benefits while scratching the “push” itch.

- Light walking and easy mobility as desired; no structured training.

- Sleep 7.5–9 hours; consistent schedule.

Here’s the finalized 1-week deload, integrating all adjustments: reduced volume/intensity, bench swap for a shoulder-friendly chest press, two Zone 2 sessions, a 20-minute mobility block, and controlled “push” exposures on Wednesday and Friday. Assumes a 4-day U/L split and the same exercise order/menu style from his block. Keep total working sets to 8–10 per session.

Global deload parameters
- Intensity: RPE 6–7 on all work; 3–4 RIR on compounds, 2–3 RIR on accessories.
- Volume: ~45–55% fewer sets than last week (target 8–10 sets/session).
- Tempo: 2–3 sec controlled eccentrics, smooth concentric, no grinders.
- Rest: 2–3 min compounds; 60–90 sec accessories.
- Load guide: Start ~80–85% of last week’s loads on compounds, ~75–80% on accessories; adjust to stay within RPE.
- Warm-up: 2–3 ramp sets to first work set; shoulder prep before upper days (band ER 2×12, face pulls 2×15, wall slides 1–2×8).

Week overview
- Day 1: Upper (horizontal) with shoulder-friendly bench swap
- Day 2: Lower (squat focus)
- Day 3: 30 min Zone 2 + 20 min mobility
- Day 4: Upper (vertical) — controlled “push” exposure
- Day 5: Lower (hinge) — controlled “push” exposure
- Day 6: 30 min Zone 2
- Day 7: Rest

Day 1 – Upper (horizontal emphasis; bench swap)
- Primary horizontal press (pick one that’s pain-free): Neutral-grip DB floor press OR converging machine chest press
  • If floor/Smith variant: 3 sets × 3–5 reps @ RPE 6
  • If machine/DB press: 2–3 sets × 6–8 reps @ RPE 6–7
  • Guardrails: Neutral grip, elbows ~30–60°, cap bottom ROM before shoulder pinch.
- Row (same variant as block): 2–3 × 6–8 @ RPE 6–7
- Secondary press (incline DB or low-incline cable press, neutral grip): 1–2 × 8–10 @ RPE 6–7; skip if provocative
- Horizontal row (chest-supported/cable): 1–2 × 10–12 @ RPE 6–7
- Lateral raise: 1 × 12–15 @ RPE 6–7
- Triceps isolation: 0–1 × 10–12 @ RPE 6–7
Total sets: 8–10

Day 2 – Lower (squat focus)
- Back squat (same variant): 3 × 3–5 @ RPE 6
- Hip hinge accessory (RDL/hamstring hinge): 2 × 6–8 @ RPE 6–7
- Split squat or leg press: 1–2 × 8–10 @ RPE 6–7
- Leg curl: 1–2 × 10–12 @ RPE 6–7
- Calf raise: 1 × 10–12 @ RPE 6–7
- Optional easy core: 0–1 easy set (stop well short of fatigue)
Total sets: 8–10

Day 3 – Active recovery
- Zone 2 cardio: 30 minutes at conversational pace (60–70% HRmax, RPE 3–4). Modalities: incline walk, bike, elliptical; keep shoulder relaxed.
- Mobility session (20 minutes, light, smooth, pain-free):
  • 90/90 hip lift with reach: 2×5–6 breaths
  • Sidelying open books: 1–2×6–8/side
  • Wall slides with lift-off: 2×6–8
  • Banded external rotations (30–45° abduction): 2×12–15
  • Prone Y/T/W (thumbs up): 1–2×6 each
  • Serratus punches: 2×10–12
  • Scap push-ups (wall/high incline): 2×8–10
  • Hip 90/90 switches: 1–2×6–8/side
  • Half-kneeling hip flexor + glute squeeze: 1–2×20–30 sec/side
  • Knee-over-toe ankle rocks: 1–2×8–10/side
  • Child’s pose with side reach: 1×4–5 breaths/side

Day 4 – Upper (vertical emphasis) — controlled push day
Guardrails for push exposure: One top exposure only; cap at RPE 7; replace other sets to keep total ≤10.
- Primary vertical press (choose pain-free variant: OHP, landmine press, or machine shoulder press, neutral grips)
  • Top single @ RPE 6–7, then 1 back-off set of 3–5 @ RPE 6–7
- Vertical pull (pull-up or pulldown): 2–3 × 6–8 @ RPE 6–7
- Optional horizontal press power primer (shoulder-friendly variant): 3–4 × 3 reps @ ~60% usual load, fast but controlled; 60–75 sec rest
- Row/high row: 1–2 × 10–12 @ RPE 6–7
- Rear delts/face pulls: 1 × 12–15 @ RPE 6–7
- Arms: 0–1 × 10–12 @ RPE 6–7
Total sets: 8–10

Day 5 – Lower (hinge emphasis) — controlled push day
Guardrails for push exposure: One top exposure only; cap at RPE 7; replace other sets to keep total ≤10.
- Deadlift (same variant)
  • Top single @ RPE 6–7, then 1 back-off set of 2–3 @ RPE 6
- Secondary squat (front squat or high-bar): 2 × 4–6 @ RPE 6–7
- Hip thrust or glute bridge: 1–2 × 8–10 @ RPE 6–7
- Leg extension: 1–2 × 10–12 @ RPE 6–7
- Calf raise: 1 × 12–15 @ RPE 6–7
- Optional conditioning flair (only if legs feel fresh): 6–8 × 10-sec relaxed bike sprints, 50-sec easy spin; keep HR mostly Zone 2/low Zone 3. Skip if any fatigue.
Total sets: 8–10

Day 6 – Zone 2 cardio
- 30 minutes at conversational pace (RPE 3–4). Choose a shoulder-friendly modality. Separate from lifting days by 6–8 hours if you had to shift it.

Day 7 – Rest
- Light walking and easy mobility as desired; no structured training.

Strength/readiness markers (embedded, low fatigue)
- Day 4: Primary vertical press top single @ RPE 6–7 + back-off 3–5 @ RPE 6–7; log load, RPE, pain-free ROM.
- Day 5: Deadlift top single @ RPE 6–7 + back-off 2–3 @ RPE 6; log load, RPE, bar speed notes.
- Optional (Day 2 or 1): If desired, add squat top single @ RPE 6 before the 3×3–5, replacing one squat set to keep total ≤10.

Recovery and nutrition
- Sleep 7.5–9 hours; consistent schedule.
- Steps: 6–10k/day.
- Protein 1.6–2.2 g/kg/day; carbs sufficient to feel fueled; hydration 35–40 ml/kg/day; sodium 3–5 g/day unless contraindicated.
- Pain/technique guardrails: Stop any set that provokes shoulder pain; neutral grips and ROM caps for pressing; crisp reps only.

Notes on execution
- If any “push” exposure creeps above RPE 7 or bar speed slows, shut it down and continue deload work.
- Keep total per-session working sets at 8–10; the “push” exposures replace other sets, they do not add on.
- Finish each session feeling better than you started—freshness is the goal heading into next week’s intensification.
